11. Design Overview

LayerImplementationNotes
LocomotionKinematic freejoint No joint-torque instability; fast headless eval
Perception16-ray 270° LiDAR ring Sparse; sufficient for corridors
LocalisationSeeded gyro-noise dead-reckoning No GT; deterministic per seed; no loop closure
MappingKnown OG for planning; sensor OG for safety GT map drives A*; LiDAR map drives collision check
PlanningA* → corridor-centred waypoints Globally optimal, orthogonal path
ControlPure-pursuit + forward slowdown Smooth; reactive to heading error

12. Dominant Failure Mode

All timeouts trace to localisation drift causing goal misdetection.

  1. Yaw accumulation. Gyro noise (σ=0.005 rad/s, seeded) integrates linearly; over 200 s heading error ≈ ±1°, displacing position ~0.15 m per 10 m of travel.
  2. Collision discontinuities. The kinematic resolver jumps the robot; the localiser (commanded-velocity) misses the jump, injecting a fixed error per contact event.

Secondary: tight U-turns in dead-ends — pure-pursuit is slow to reverse, and accumulated drift can trap the robot in a corner.

13. Tradeoffs

TradeoffChoiceCost
Kinematic vs physicsKinematicOptimistic — no falls
Dead-reckoning vs SLAMDead-reckoningUnbounded drift
Known map vs SLAMKnown mapNot generalisable
16-ray LiDAR vs dense16 raysMisses narrow gaps
Pure-pursuit vs MPCPure-pursuitOvershoots corners
Inflation R=3 cells0.3 m clearanceConservative but safe

14. Verdict — Would you trust this robot unsupervised?

Not yet — but close for small, short mazes.

What works

  • Held-out solve rate 100% (95% CI 87%–100%) on 10×10.
  • Zero stuck events across all 25 episodes — pure-pursuit + corridor-centering is robust in this maze size.
  • ATE RMSE <0.05 m mean; drift <0.1% of path — odometry is accurate for runs up to ~200 s.
  • Real-time factor >30× — well within any real-time budget.
  • Structurally deterministic (seed ⇒ identical run) and crash-safe (HDF5 readable after SIGKILL).

What doesn't

  • Drift is unbounded. No correction mechanism; failure risk rises with episode length.
  • No recovery planner. A stuck or off-path robot has no replanning trigger.
  • Kinematic locomotion is optimistic. A real G1 must balance; gait jitter would worsen localisation and increase collisions.

Conditions for safe unsupervised operation

  1. Maze ≤ 10×10, path ≤ 15 m.
  2. ICP scan-matching against known map to bound drift <0.2 m.
  3. Replanning trigger: rerun A* if no goal progress in 15 s.
